summary.coreClaim: Professional and therapy-room games hide inside helping relationships where the helper's role provides structural cover. Three patterns (ITHY, Wooden Leg, Greenhouse), all requiring helper complicity. Diagnosing requires looking at both sides because the helper is part of the game.
anchorsUsed: Ife and Rémy's three-year supervision arrangement
Bo and Caleb's two-year learning disability pattern
Tamsin and Zara's two-year Greenhouse therapy
summary.hardDepthTension: The helper is part of the game. The professional role is the cover. Diagnosing requires the helper to ask what they have been getting, which professional training does not teach.
summary.bridgeToNextChapter: Not all games are destructive. The next chapter covers the ones whose net effect is positive even when structure is ulterior.

strongestQualities: The Wooden Leg anchor holds the real-limitation complexity without moralizing or denying; the 'both realities in one sentence' antithesis is the chapter's most practically useful move.
The helper-is-part-of-the-game structural claim in P6 is the distinguishing argument that makes this chapter different from every other catalog chapter.
All three anchors are contemporary helping-profession contexts (supervision, student success, therapy) rather than the dated 1964 consulting-room examples, with Indigence explicitly avoided.
